rules.sentence: Computed tomography (CT) is the best imaging modality for a left upper quadrant process, and will reveal the air-fluid level with wall enhancement.
Ultrasound also demonstrates a heterogeneous fluid collection containing gas and debris and is frequently used to diagnose right-sided collections.
Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and an indium-111-labeled leukocyte scan may be helpful for an occult intra-abdominal or subphrenic abscess.
MR enterography is the investigation of choice in patients with active inflammatory bowel disease and possible abscess.
In pregnant patients with suspected acute intra-abdominal abscess, ultrasound or MRI can be considered as the initial diagnostic imaging modality.
Initial management of a subphrenic abscess consists of resuscitation as indicated.
Supportive and therapeutic care includes broad-spectrum antibiotics, fluid replenishment, mechanical and pharmacologic adjuncts for any decrement in oxygenation.
Patients who are hypoxic, hemodynamically unstable, or obtunded may require mechanical ventilation and pharmacologic hemodynamic support until their condition stabilizes.
